evals.prompt: With dotnet-patterns loaded, implement a small behaviour change in a C# project in a target repo (e.g. add a method that validates input and can fail).
evals.expected_output: A scoped change that honours nullable reference types (no ! suppression), disposes IDisposable via using, adds xUnit/NUnit tests covering the behaviour plus a boundary and an exception case, compiles cleanly, and applies standard C# formatting.
assertions: Nullable reference types are honoured (no `!` null-forgiving suppression to silence warnings)
xUnit/NUnit tests cover the happy path plus a boundary and an exception case
The code compiles cleanly on inspection (no missing usings, undefined symbols, or type errors) and follows standard C# formatting
No existing test is weakened, skipped, or deleted

evals.prompt: With dotnet-patterns loaded, add asynchronous code that calls an external service.
evals.expected_output: Async all the way (no .Result/.Wait()), ConfigureAwait(false) in library code, a CancellationToken flowing through, and deterministic tests; no async void.
assertions: Async all the way: no blocking on async via .Result or .Wait(), and no async void (except event handlers)
Library code uses ConfigureAwait(false) and a CancellationToken is accepted/propagated
Tests are deterministic (no real network/clock; the clock is faked if used)
IDisposable/IAsyncDisposable resources from the call are disposed (using / await using)

component.purpose: The .NET (C#) conventions and toolchain the software-engineer/qa-engineer (and the code-review lint aspect) apply when the detected stack is .NET; a lean, loaded-on-demand knowledge pack exercised through the software-engineer's Tier-2.
